newsitem.title: USA: FCOJ Jan futures retrace gains to end weaker.
newsitem.headline: FCOJ Jan futures retrace gains to end weaker.

text.p: NYCE January frozen concentrated orange juice futures failed to sustain recent gains and ended the day lower, pressured by mostly trade selling, dealers said.
The back months closed barely firmer, however.
January juice ended 0.35 lower at 90.85, traded 91.60 to 90.30 cents. The back months settled 0.25 lower to 0.60 higher.
Volume was estimated at 2,000 lots, compared with Tuesday's official volume of 3,437 lots.
Paine Webber analyst Bernard Savaiko said that with the impending cold weather and prices appearing oversold on the charts, "the bears may have second thoughts about overstaying their welcome."

But temperatures across the Florida citrus belt are not likely to dip into dangerous territory in the near term. Smith Barney meteorologist Jon Davis said a recent cool air mass is moving into the Atlantic Ocean and temperatures will warm through Saturday.
Savaiko said that without the threat of frost in the next two weeks, the market could dip to between 83.10 and 82.50 basis the January contract.
What's more, "there has been enough damage on the charts that I would think twice about proclaiming a bottom just yet," he said.
